name: Ben Balter
milestone_by_age_26: No material career-defining milestone by age 26 firmly established. Selected as an inaugural Presidential Innovation Fellow (2011–2013) and joined GitHub as Government Evangelist in March 2013 around age 25–26, but primary public impact and leadership roles accumulated later across a decade at GitHub.
early_history_summary: Earned a BA in political science from George Washington University (2009) and JD/MBA from GW (2013). Served as FCC New Media Fellow, then inaugural Presidential Innovation Fellow helping draft the Digital Government Strategy, before joining GitHub in 2013.
evidence_summary: Balter completed dual JD/MBA credentials and held early federal tech roles including the inaugural PIF class, then joined GitHub as Government Evangelist in 2013. While the White House fellowship and GitHub hire are notable, they do not clearly meet the bar of a material, independently breakout milestone by 26 comparable to founding a major product or publishing foundational research; later GitHub leadership defines his public profile.

name: Kyle Daigle
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 verified. Birth year not documented in reviewed sources; joined GitHub around 2013 and later became COO, but age at early career steps cannot be confirmed.
early_history_summary: Began coding as a teenager (reported starting at 13, building tools for a local election office). Worked on startups and Rails projects while briefly studying lighting design, then joined GitHub as a developer and rose through engineering leadership to COO.
family_context_summary: Grew up in rural Connecticut (farm side, not NYC-adjacent). Family financial background not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents reportedly wanted him to study computer science (Connecticut insurance-industry path); not domain experts in startups or open-source platforms.
evidence_summary: Daigle has a strong multi-year GitHub career culminating in COO, with early coding from age 13 documented in interviews, but without a verified birth year the age-26 eligibility gate cannot be passed. No independently dated breakout product founding or research milestone by a confirmed age ≤26 was found.

name: Shaowen Bardzell
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Earned a comparative-literature PhD in 2004 after a 1991 BA and 1994 MA; defining HCI contribution (Feminist HCI paper) was published in 2010, well after age 26 even under generous birth-year estimates.
early_history_summary: Taiwanese-American scholar who earned a BA in foreign languages and literatures at Tunghai University (1991), then MA (1994) and PhD in comparative literature (2004) at Indiana University Bloomington before transitioning into informatics and HCI faculty roles.
evidence_summary: Bardzell's academic path ran through literature degrees into HCI; the widely cited Feminist HCI paper (2010) and later CHI Academy recognition came in mid-career. Birth year is not published; no dated material CS/HCI milestone by age 26 is identifiable.

name: Alex Larsson
milestone_by_age_26: No clear material breakout milestone by age 26. First GNOME contribution around 1998 (~age 23–24) and joined Red Hat in 2001 (~age 26–27); defining work on Flatpak and major desktop infrastructure came later.
early_history_summary: Swedish developer from Stockholm who began contributing to GNOME (Dia) in 1998 while in university, then joined Red Hat in 2001 and spent decades on GNOME, GTK, Nautilus, GIO, Docker infrastructure, and Flatpak.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Born in Stockholm, Sweden.
evidence_summary: A 2005 FOSDEM interview states Larsson was 30, implying birth around 1974–1975. Early open-source contributions and a Red Hat hire near age 26–27 are solid early-career steps but not a single dated material breakout comparable to product founding or foundational research; Flatpak and major GNOME leadership came later.

name: Caterina Fake
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Graduated Vassar in 1991 (~age 22) and worked various jobs; joined Netscape community forums in 1997 at age ~28; co-founded Flickr in 2004 at age 34–35.
early_history_summary: Born in Pittsburgh and raised in northern New Jersey by an American father and Filipina mother; attended Choate and Vassar (English). Taught herself web design in San Francisco after college, later working at Salon and Netscape before co-founding Ludicorp/Flickr with Stewart Butterfield.
family_context_summary: Raised in northern New Jersey by an American father and Filipina mother; childhood emphasized reading poetry and classical music rather than television.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as technology-domain parents in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Fake's defining achievement—co-founding Flickr and the subsequent Yahoo acquisition and Web 2.0 influence—occurred in her mid-30s. Early career at Netscape (1997, age ~28) already exceeds the age-26 cutoff; no independently verified material milestone by 26 was found.

name: Donna Auguste
milestone_by_age_26: No material career-defining milestone by age 26 found. First African-American woman to enter CMU CS PhD program (~early 1980s, age ~24–25) is notable academically, but industry milestones (IntelliCorp 1986, Apple Newton leadership ~1990, Freshwater Software 1996) all occurred after age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Texas (1958), raised by a single mother with four sisters; loved disassembling appliances as a child. Earned EECS BS from UC Berkeley, entered CMU CS PhD as the first African-American woman in the program, then joined IntelliCorp (1986) and later led Newton software engineering at Apple.
family_context_summary: Born in Texas; raised with four sisters by their mother (Willie Mae Fruge; father described as a restaurateur in some profiles). Relocated across Louisiana and California.
evidence_summary: Auguste overcame significant barriers as a Black woman in EECS and entered CMU's CS PhD program first among African-American women, but her material industry milestones—IntelliCorp hire (age ~28), Apple Newton leadership (age ~32), and Freshwater Software founding/sale (age ~38–42)—all postdate 26.

name: Rafał Józefowicz
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed material milestone by age 26. Competed in TopCoder High School finals in 2007 (handle rlp); later co-authored Google Brain language-modeling work (2016) and worked at OpenAI (2016–2018). Birth year not published; 2016 research was likely past age 26 given 2007 high-school status.
early_history_summary: Polish competitive programmer (TopCoder handle rlp) who reached TCHS 2007 finals with ~2000 rating; later worked in finance, deep learning at Google Brain, OpenAI research (including language models and OpenAI Five era), then D.E. Shaw.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Grew up in Olsztyn, Poland (per TopCoder program bio).
evidence_summary: High-school TopCoder finals (2007) demonstrate early competitive-programming skill but are not alone a material career breakout. Google/OpenAI language-model work around 2016 cannot be firmly dated to age ≤26 without a birth year; conservative ruling is ineligible.

English Wikipedia page for 'Steve Gill' refers to a conservative talk-radio host (born 1956), not a PhoneGap engineer; no independently verifiable PhoneGap/Nitobi/Cordova engineer matching this curation was located with dated early milestones.

evidence_summary: The curated Wikipedia URL resolves to an unrelated radio host. No second source establishes a PhoneGap engineer named Steve Gill with a dated ≤26 milestone; treated as age_26_ineligible for lack of verifiable early material achievement.

name: Alec Radford
milestone_by_age_26: Lead author of OpenAI's 2018 generative pre-training paper introducing GPT (foundational to ChatGPT) at age 25, after joining OpenAI around 2016 at age ~23 and co-founding AI startup Indico while at Olin College.
early_history_summary: Born April 1993 and raised in the Dallas–Fort Worth area; Eagle Scout and 2011 graduate of Cistercian Preparatory School. Attended Olin College, co-founded Indico with classmates in a dorm room, dropped out in 2014 to scale the startup, then joined early OpenAI in 2016 and drove foundational GPT, CLIP, Whisper, and DALL·E work.
family_context_summary: Grew up in the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex in Texas. Family financial and parental occupational details not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Indico cofounders, Olin College, Kaggle competitions, early OpenAI, GPT lead author, deep learning wave
evidence_summary: Radford and peers at Olin co-founded Indico after bonding over late-night ML work and Kaggle competitions; DCGAN-era research at Indico (with FAIR mentorship) established him before OpenAI. Joining OpenAI in 2016 at ~23 placed him in a scarce early-lab network as deep learning scaled; lead authorship of the 2018 GPT paper at 25 was a clear material milestone. Family background is sparsely documented; advantages center on peer cofounders, online competition platforms, and immersion in the deep-learning structural wave rather than inherited capital or parental domain.
starting_point: Born April 1993 and raised in the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex, Texas; family class and parental occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Independent AI researcher and advisor to Thinking Machines Lab after leaving OpenAI in December 2024; co-released Talkie (pre-1930-trained model) in 2026.

trajectory.event: Graduated from Cistercian Preparatory School as an Eagle Scout and entered Olin College of Engineering.
Dropped out of Olin to scale Indico, the AI startup he co-founded with classmates in a dorm room.
Joined early OpenAI as a research scientist after Indico's generative-image work gained industry attention.
Lead author of OpenAI's generative pre-training paper introducing GPT, foundation of later ChatGPT models.
Co-authored major multimodal work including CLIP and contributed to DALL·E and related generative systems.
Left OpenAI in December to pursue independent research after nearly a decade of foundational model work.
Joined Thinking Machines Lab as an advisor alongside other former OpenAI leaders.

name: Joseph J. Allaire
milestone_by_age_26: Created ColdFusion and co-founded Allaire Corporation with brother Jeremy in May 1995 at age 25, launching a pioneering web application server and company that later IPO'd (1999) and was acquired by Macromedia (2001).
early_history_summary: Born September 27, 1969 in South Bend, Indiana; raised partly in Winona, Minnesota in a family that valued progressive activism and acquired an early Apple computer in 1983. Graduated Macalester College (political science/economics) in 1991, then created ColdFusion and founded Allaire Corp. in 1995 with brother Jeremy using about $18,000 of his savings.
family_context_summary: Parents Jim (psychologist) and Barb (press editor); progressive/activist household. Family moved to Winona, Minnesota; acquired an early Apple computer around 1983 that sparked the brothers' computing interest.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not software entrepreneurs; domain advantage came more from sibling partnership and early home computer access than parental industry fluency.
primary_early_advantage_tags: brother cofounder Jeremy, early Apple at home, ColdFusion 1995, web application wave, Macalester
evidence_summary: JJ Allaire and brother Jeremy co-founded Allaire Corporation in 1995 when JJ was 25, creating ColdFusion to make database-driven websites far easier to build—an early product insight riding the web wave. Family provided an early personal computer and progressive intellectual climate but not tech-industry capital or networks; the high-trust sibling partnership and modest self-funding ($18k savings) were central. Subsequent ventures (Onfolio, Lose It!, RStudio/Posit, Inspect AI) show serial product-building capacity rooted in that early founding.
starting_point: Born September 27, 1969 in South Bend, Indiana; raised in a progressive household (father psychologist, mother press editor) that later moved to Winona, Minnesota and acquired an early Apple computer.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Posit (formerly RStudio); also led development of Inspect AI at the UK AI Security Institute; serial entrepreneur across web tools, health apps, and data science platforms.

trajectory.event: Graduated from Macalester College with a bachelor's degree in political science and economics.
Created ColdFusion and co-founded Allaire Corporation with brother Jeremy in Minneapolis.
Allaire Corporation completed its IPO as ColdFusion became a major web development platform.
Allaire Corporation was acquired by Macromedia for about $360 million.
Co-founded FitNow and launched the Lose It! weight-loss app, later reaching tens of millions of users.
Founded RStudio (later Posit) to build open-source tools for the R statistical computing ecosystem.
Joined the UK AI Security Institute as a staff engineer and led open-sourcing of the Inspect AI evaluation framework.

name: Larry Osterman
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 verified. Long-tenured Microsoft engineer known for Windows audio (decades of work including Windows sound subsystem); interviewed at MIT around 1989 and has ~40 years at Microsoft, but birth year and any dated ≤26 breakout are not documented in reviewed sources.
early_history_summary: Longtime Microsoft principal software design engineer associated with Windows audio and related systems; public interviews emphasize multi-decade Microsoft tenure rather than a youthful breakout product or paper.
evidence_summary: Osterman is a well-known internal Microsoft engineer and blogger on Windows audio history, but public sources do not establish birth year or a specific dated material milestone at age ≤26. Career recognition is cumulative over decades rather than an early breakout.

name: Margrit Betke
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Earned MIT PhD in CS/EE in 1995 under Ron Rivest at about age 28; major contributions (Camera Mouse, medical image analysis patents, BU professorship) came in the late 1990s–2000s.
early_history_summary: German-American computer scientist born in Langenhagen, Germany, and raised in St. Augustin; completed PhD at MIT in 1995, then built a career at Boston University in computer vision, assistive interfaces (Camera Mouse with James Gips), and medical imaging. Died August 13, 2025 at age 58.
family_context_summary: Born in Langenhagen, Germany; grew up in St. Augustin. Family financial and parental occupational details not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Obituary age (58 in 2025) implies birth ~1966–1967, so MIT PhD in 1995 was around age 28—already past the age-26 gate. Camera Mouse and patented pulmonary-nodule algorithms are significant but post-26 achievements.
